quote_orig: וְעַתָּ֡ה שְׁנֵֽי־בָנֶ֩יךָ֩ הַנּוֹלָדִ֨ים לְךָ֜ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם עַד־בֹּאִ֥י אֵלֶ֛יךָ מִצְרַ֖יְמָה לִי־הֵ֑ם אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ וּמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה כִּרְאוּבֵ֥ן וְשִׁמְע֖וֹן יִֽהְיוּ־לִֽי׃ וּמוֹלַדְתְּךָ֛ אֲשֶׁר־הוֹלַ֥דְתָּ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם לְךָ֣ יִהְי֑וּ עַ֣ל שֵׁ֧ם אֲחֵיהֶ֛ם יִקָּרְא֖וּ בְּנַחֲלָתָֽם׃
quote_en: And now thy two sons, who were born unto thee in the land of Egypt before I came unto thee into Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh, even as Reuben and Simeon, shall be mine. And thy issue, that thou begettest after them, shall be thine; they shall be called after the name of their brethren in their inheritance.
licence_note: Hebrew: MAM (Sefaria) licence CC-BY-SA. English: JPS 1917, Public Domain (Sefaria metadata).
from_: And now thy two sons, who were
to: name of their brethren in their inheritance.
what_it_shows: Jacob tells Joseph that Joseph's two sons born in Egypt 'are mine' as Reuben and Simeon are, and that Joseph's later children will be 'called after the name of their brethren in their inheritance'. The verses count Joseph's sons as Jacob's own for name and inheritance.
context: Jacob, dying in Egypt, addresses Joseph before blessing the boys (the crossed-hands blessing is at 48:14-20, read). Joseph is their father by birth (41:50-52, read), so they are Jacob's grandsons by blood.
limits: (1) The adoptees are Jacob's own grandsons by blood, and the declaration is a grandfather's reckoning of blood grandsons, not the adoption of an unrelated outsider. (2) 48:5-6 never uses a word meaning 'adopt' and does not state a mechanism. (3) 48:6 gives the later children to Joseph ('shall be thine'), reckoned under their brothers' names: they do not become Jacob's sons. (4) The hint's phrase 'giving each a tribal share' is NOT in 48:5-6; the share is in Josh 16-17 and Num 1:32-35 (read). Num 1:32 and Josh 16:4 call them 'the children of Joseph'. (5) Rashi on 48:6 (Rosenbaum & Silbermann, Public Domain; Hebrew translated by the team, not from Sefaria): later children 'will not be counted among my sons, but will be included within the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, and will have no name among the tribes for purposes of inheritance'. Rashi's English on the same comment (Public Domain) says: 'yet only these of Joseph's sons bore the name of "tribe"'. (6) Gen 48:22 (read): Jacob gives Joseph 'one aportion above thy brethren'. (7) Counter-text: Gen 15:2-4 (read): Abram's house-born Eliezer is not heir: 'This man shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.' (8) Rashi on 48:5 (commentator, verified) reads 'they shall be counted amongst my other sons, to receive a portion in the Land each for himself'.

quote_orig: הַמַּלְאָךְ֩ הַגֹּאֵ֨ל אֹתִ֜י מִכׇּל־רָ֗ע יְבָרֵךְ֮ אֶת־הַנְּעָרִים֒ וְיִקָּרֵ֤א בָהֶם֙ שְׁמִ֔י וְשֵׁ֥ם אֲבֹתַ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם וְיִצְחָ֑ק וְיִדְגּ֥וּ לָרֹ֖ב בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
quote_en: the angel who hath redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named in them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth.’
from_: the angel who hath redeemed me from
to: multitude in the midst of the earth.’
what_it_shows: Jacob blesses the boys and asks that 'my name' and 'the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac' be named upon them.
context: Part of Jacob's blessing of Joseph's sons (48:14-20). The verse follows his declaration in 48:5-6 that the boys are his.
limits: The verse is a blessing about names. It says nothing about tribe, lineage or inheritance; inheritance appears only in 48:6. It does not say that carrying a name changes legal status.

quote_orig: וּבְנֵ֨י רְאוּבֵ֥ן בְּכֽוֹר־יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ כִּ֣י ה֣וּא הַבְּכוֹר֒ וּֽבְחַלְּלוֹ֙ יְצוּעֵ֣י אָבִ֔יו נִתְּנָה֙ בְּכֹ֣רָת֔וֹ לִבְנֵ֥י יוֹסֵ֖ף בֶּן־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֥א לְהִתְיַחֵ֖שׂ לַבְּכֹרָֽה׃ כִּ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ גָּבַ֣ר בְּאֶחָ֔יו וּלְנָגִ֖יד מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְהַבְּכֹרָ֖ה לְיוֹסֵֽף׃
quote_en: And the sons of Reuben the first-born of Israel—for he was the first-born; but, forasmuch as he defiled his father’s couch, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph the son of Israel, yet not so that he was to be reckoned in the genealogy as first-born. For Judah prevailed above his brethren, and of him came he that is the prince; but the birthright was Joseph’s—
from_: And the sons of Reuben the first-born
to: the prince; but the birthright was Joseph’s—
what_it_shows: The Chronicler says Reuben's birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, so Reuben is not reckoned as firstborn in the genealogy. The same verse gives leadership ('the prince') to Judah, while the birthright goes to Joseph.
context: Opening of the genealogy of Israel's tribes. It explains Reuben's forfeiture by the defilement of his father's couch (see Gen 35:22 and Gen 49:3-4, read).
limits: The verse does not say 'adopted' and does not mention Jacob's blessing (its basis is Gen 48:22 and the Jacob-Reuben story). The Joseph sons are called 'sons of Joseph, son of Israel', i.e. Joseph's sons. Crucially, 5:2 separates the birthright (to Joseph) from rule: 'For Judah prevailed above his brethren, and of him came he that is the prince; but the birthright was Joseph's'. A transfer of birthright did not transfer royal lineage.

quote_orig: וַֽיְדַבְּרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ לֵאמֹ֑ר מַדּ֩וּעַ֩ נָתַ֨תָּה לִּ֜י נַחֲלָ֗ה גּוֹרָ֤ל אֶחָד֙ וְחֶ֣בֶל אֶחָ֔ד וַאֲנִ֣י עַם־רָ֔ב עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר־עַד־כֹּ֖ה בֵּרְכַ֥נִי יְהֹוָֽה׃ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ אִם־עַם־רַ֤ב אַתָּה֙ עֲלֵ֣ה לְךָ֣ הַיַּ֔עְרָה וּבֵרֵאתָ֤ לְךָ֙ שָׁ֔ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הַפְּרִזִּ֖י וְהָרְפָאִ֑ים כִּי־אָ֥ץ לְךָ֖ הַר־אֶפְרָֽיִם׃ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף לֹא־יִמָּ֥צֵא לָ֖נוּ הָהָ֑ר וְרֶ֣כֶב בַּרְזֶ֗ל בְּכׇל־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ הַיֹּשֵׁ֣ב בְּאֶרֶץ־הָעֵ֔מֶק לַאֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּבֵית־שְׁאָן֙ וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְלַאֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֥מֶק יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף לְאֶפְרַ֥יִם וְלִמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר עַם־רַ֣ב אַתָּ֗ה וְכֹ֤חַ גָּדוֹל֙ לָ֔ךְ לֹֽא־יִֽהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֖ גּוֹרָ֥ל אֶחָֽד׃
quote_en: And the children of Joseph spoke unto Joshua, saying: ‘Why hast thou given me but one lot and one part for an inheritance, seeing I am a great people, forasmuch as the LORD hath blessed me thus?’ And Joshua said unto them: ‘If thou be a great people, get thee up to the forest, and cut down for thyself there in the land of the Perizzites and of the Rephaim; since the hill-country of Ephraim is too narrow for thee.’ And the children of Joseph said: ‘The hill-country will not be enough for us; and all the Canaanites that dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron, both they who are in Beth-shean and its towns, and they who are in the valley of Jezreel.’ And Joshua spoke unto the house of Joseph, even to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying: ‘Thou art a great people, and hast great power; thou shalt not have one lot only;
from_: And the children of Joseph spoke unto
to: thou shalt not have one lot only;
keys: מַדּ֩וּעַ֩ נָתַ֨תָּה לִּ֜י נַחֲלָ֗ה גּוֹרָ֤ל אֶחָד֙
what_it_shows: 'The children of Joseph' ask Joshua why they got only 'one lot and one part'; Joshua answers 'the house of Joseph, even to Ephraim and to Manasseh' that they shall not have one lot only, and that 'the hill-country shall be thine' (17:17-18).
context: Allotment of the tribe of Manasseh and of Ephraim (ch. 16-17). Josh 17:1 (read): 'for he was the first-born of Joseph' is said of Manasseh; Josh 16:4 (read): 'the children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance'.
limits: The text calls the claimants 'children of Joseph' (17:14) and Manasseh 'the first-born of Joseph' (17:1), not Jacob's sons. Joshua does not mention adoption; the tribal status is presupposed from Gen 48. Num 1:32-35 (read) also says 'Of the children of Joseph, namely, of the children of Ephraim'. No Jacob-based rule is stated in this passage.

quote_orig: וְהָיָ֗ה תַּפִּ֣לוּ אוֹתָהּ֮ בְּנַחֲלָה֒ לָכֶ֗ם וּלְהַגֵּרִים֙ הַגָּרִ֣ים בְּתוֹכְכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹלִ֥דוּ בָנִ֖ים בְּתוֹכְכֶ֑ם וְהָי֣וּ לָכֶ֗ם כְּאֶזְרָח֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִתְּכֶם֙ יִפְּל֣וּ בְנַֽחֲלָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וְהָיָ֣ה בַשֵּׁ֔בֶט אֲשֶׁר־גָּ֥ר הַגֵּ֖ר אִתּ֑וֹ שָׁ֚ם תִּתְּנ֣וּ נַחֲלָת֔וֹ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יֱהֹוִֽה׃
quote_en: And it shall come to pass, that ye shall divide it by lot for an inheritance unto you and to the strangers that sojourn among you, who shall beget children among you; and they shall be unto you as the home-born among the children of Israel; they shall have inheritance with you among the tribes of Israel. And it shall come to pass, that in what tribe the stranger sojourneth, there shall ye give him his inheritance, saith the Lord GOD.
from_: And it shall come to pass, that
to: him his inheritance, saith the Lord GOD.
what_it_shows: A resident stranger (ger) is to be treated 'as the home-born among the children of Israel' and given an inheritance 'in what tribe the stranger sojourneth'. This is a rule for incorporating outsiders into a tribe.
context: Part of the land-division instructions (47:21: 'So shall ye divide this land unto you according to the tribes of Israel'), in the vision of the restored land (Ezek 40-48).
limits: (1) It is a prophetic vision of the future land, not a description of past practice. (2) The same prophet excludes aliens from the sanctuary: 'No alien, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into My sanctuary' (44:9, read). (3) The stranger's status comes from residence and birth 'among you' (47:22: 'who shall beget children among you'), not from adoption, a legal father or a name. The verse never calls the stranger a son.

quote_orig: וַיַּ֤רְא יוֹסֵף֙ לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם בְּנֵ֖י שִׁלֵּשִׁ֑ים גַּ֗ם בְּנֵ֤י מָכִיר֙ בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יֻלְּד֖וּ עַל־בִּרְכֵּ֥י יוֹסֵֽף׃
quote_en: And Joseph saw Ephraim’s children of the third generation; the children also of Machir the son of Manasseh were born upon Joseph’s knees.
from_: And Joseph saw Ephraim’s children of the
to: of Manasseh were born upon Joseph’s knees.
what_it_shows: Joseph sees Ephraim's children of the third generation, and 'the children also of Machir the son of Manasseh were born upon Joseph's knees'.
context: Verse 50:23 is read on its own (50:22 and 50:24-26 not read). Machir is Manasseh's son, so Machir's children are Joseph's great-grandchildren.
limits: The phrase 'born upon the knees' is used for children who are not Joseph's by birth: they are Machir's. The verse does not say Joseph adopted them or that they are counted as his sons. Machir is still 'the son of Manasseh' here, and 'the first-born of Manasseh' in Josh 17:1 (read). The phrase matches Gen 30:3 (Bilhah), where Rashi and Onkelos read 'I will rear them' (see A1-P07). Its legal meaning is not explained in the verse.

quote_orig: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה אֲמָתִ֥י בִלְהָ֖ה בֹּ֣א אֵלֶ֑יהָ וְתֵלֵד֙ עַל־בִּרְכַּ֔י וְאִבָּנֶ֥ה גַם־אָנֹכִ֖י מִמֶּֽנָּה׃ וַתִּתֶּן־ל֛וֹ אֶת־בִּלְהָ֥ה שִׁפְחָתָ֖הּ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֥א אֵלֶ֖יהָ יַעֲקֹֽב׃
quote_en: And she said: ‘Behold my maid Bilhah, go in unto her; that she may bear upon my knees, and I also may be builded up through her.’ And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid to wife; and Jacob went in unto her.
licence_note: MAM CC-BY-SA; JPS 1917 Public Domain. Onkelos (CC-BY-NC) and Rashi (PD) cited in limits only.
from_: And she said: ‘Behold my maid Bilhah,
to: wife; and Jacob went in unto her.
what_it_shows: Rachel gives her maid Bilhah to Jacob so that Bilhah 'may bear upon my knees' and Rachel 'may be builded up through her'. Bilhah bears a son (Dan), whom Rachel names (30:5-6).
context: Rachel's and Leah's rivalry over children (30:1-24). The maid-child formula is repeated for Zilpah (30:9-13).
limits: (1) The child is Jacob's by blood: 'and Jacob went in unto her' (30:4). The formula gives the wife (Rachel) a maternal claim on her maid's child. It does not transfer a non-blood person into Jacob's line. (2) Rashi (Rosenbaum & Silbermann, Public Domain): 'UPON MY KNEES — as the Targum takes it: she will bear children and I will rear them.' (3) Targum Onkelos (Sefaria Aramaic version, licence CC-BY-NC; the English there is not quoted) reads 'אֱרַבֵּי' (I will rear) for 'upon my knees'. (4) Gen 35:23-26 (read) lists 'the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid: Dan and Naphtali' separately from 'the sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin'. (5) Reuben lay with Bilhah (35:22, read).

quote_orig: בְּנֵ֣י לֵאָ֔ה בְּכ֥וֹר יַעֲקֹ֖ב רְאוּבֵ֑ן וְשִׁמְעוֹן֙ וְלֵוִ֣י וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְיִשָּׂשכָ֖ר וּזְבֻלֽוּן׃ בְּנֵ֣י רָחֵ֔ל יוֹסֵ֖ף וּבִנְיָמִֽן׃ וּבְנֵ֤י בִלְהָה֙ שִׁפְחַ֣ת רָחֵ֔ל דָּ֖ן וְנַפְתָּלִֽי׃ וּבְנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֛ה שִׁפְחַ֥ת לֵאָ֖ה גָּ֣ד וְאָשֵׁ֑ר אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלַּד־ל֖וֹ בְּפַדַּ֥ן אֲרָֽם׃
quote_en: the sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob’s first-born, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun; the sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin; and the sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid: Dan and Naphtali; and the sons of Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid: Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, that were born to him in Paddan-aram.
from_: the sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob’s first-born,
to: that were born to him in Paddan-aram.
keys: וּבְנֵ֤י בִלְהָה֙ שִׁפְחַ֣ת רָחֵ֔ל דָּ֖ן וְנַפְתָּלִֽי׃
וּבְנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֛ה שִׁפְחַ֥ת לֵאָ֖ה גָּ֣ד וְאָשֵׁ֑ר
what_it_shows: Scripture lists 'the sons of Jacob' (twelve) as the sons of Leah, Rachel, Bilhah ('Rachel's handmaid') and Zilpah ('Leah's handmaid'), including Dan, Naphtali, Gad and Asher among them.
context: Right after Reuben lay with Bilhah (35:22). The list closes the sons of Jacob in Paddan-aram.
limits: The list keeps the handmaids' sons in a separate category ('sons of Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid'); it does not say they are counted as sons of Rachel or Leah. Their father is Jacob (Zilpah is 'given' to him as wife, 30:9, read). Reuben, who defiled his father's couch, lost the firstborn status (49:3-4, read; 1 Chr 5:1, read).

quote_orig: וַיִּגְדַּ֣ל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַתְּבִאֵ֙הוּ֙ לְבַת־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיְהִי־לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י מִן־הַמַּ֖יִם מְשִׁיתִֽהוּ׃
quote_en: And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses, and said: ‘Because I drew him out of the water.’
from_: And the child grew, and she brought
to: I drew him out of the water.’
what_it_shows: After the child grows, he is brought to 'Pharaoh's daughter' and 'he became her son' (lit. 'was to her for a son'); she names him Moses.
context: Moses' birth and rescue from the Nile (Ex 2:1-10).
limits: The verse says 'became her son' but says nothing about inheritance, lineage or tribe. Moses' Levitical descent is explicit: 'a man of the house of Levi ... took to wife a daughter of Levi' (2:1, read); his parents are listed as Levites (6:16-20, read: Amram son of Kohath son of Levi, mother Jochebed). In 2:11 (read) Moses 'went out unto his brethren'.

quote_orig: וַיְהִ֨י אֹמֵ֜ן אֶת־הֲדַסָּ֗ה הִ֤יא אֶסְתֵּר֙ בַּת־דֹּד֔וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין לָ֖הּ אָ֣ב וָאֵ֑ם וְהַנַּעֲרָ֤ה יְפַת־תֹּ֙אַר֙ וְטוֹבַ֣ת מַרְאֶ֔ה וּבְמ֤וֹת אָבִ֙יהָ֙ וְאִמָּ֔הּ לְקָחָ֧הּ מׇרְדֳּכַ֛י ל֖וֹ לְבַֽת׃
quote_en: And he brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter; for she had neither father nor mother, and the maiden was of beautiful form and fair to look on; and when her father and mother were dead, Mordecai took her for his own daughter.
from_: And he brought up Hadassah, that is,
to: Mordecai took her for his own daughter.
what_it_shows: Mordecai brings up Esther, 'his uncle's daughter', and when her parents are dead he 'took her for his own daughter'.
context: The rise of Esther to queen (2:5-18).
limits: 2:7 calls Esther Mordecai's uncle's daughter, i.e. his niece by birth. 2:15 (read) keeps her father's name: 'Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter'. The verses say nothing about her lineage or tribe, and no inheritance or status follows.

quote_orig: וַיִּקַּ֣ח הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת־שְׁ֠נֵ֠י בְּנֵ֨י רִצְפָּ֤ה בַת־אַיָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָלְדָ֣ה לְשָׁא֔וּל אֶת־אַרְמֹנִ֖י וְאֶת־מְפִבֹ֑שֶׁת וְאֶת־חֲמֵ֗שֶׁת בְּנֵי֙ מִיכַ֣ל בַּת־שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלְדָ֛ה לְעַדְרִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן־בַּרְזִלַּ֖י הַמְּחֹלָתִֽי׃
quote_en: But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite;
licence_note: MAM CC-BY-SA; JPS 1917 Public Domain. Rashi English (CC-BY) cited in limits only.
from_: But the king took the two sons
to: Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite;
what_it_shows: The verse says the king took 'the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Adriel'. Under the principle in the Talmud and Rashi the children are called after Michal because she raised them; the verse says 'bore'.
context: Gibeonite vengeance story (2 Sam 21). The plain text names Michal as the mother.
limits: (1) The plain sense is 'whom she bore' (Michal). (2) 2 Sam 6:23 (read): 'And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.' (3) 1 Sam 18:19 (read): Merab 'was given unto Adriel the Meholathite to wife'. (4) The 'raising' reading is a rabbinic and commentator resolution: Rashi on 2 Sam 21:8 (Metsudah English, CC-BY): 'It was Meirav who bore [those children] to [Adriel]... [Michal] raised them, that is why they are called by her name'. Its basis is Sanhedrin 19b (A1-P12). The verse itself does not state the principle. (5) Sanhedrin 19b records that R. Yose and R. Yehoshua ben Korha 'interpret' the verses; the commentary is exegesis, not a legal ruling on tribe or land.

quote_orig: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה נָמֵי, הָכְתִיב: ״אֶת חֲמֵשֶׁת בְּנֵי מִיכַל בַּת שָׁאוּל״? אָמַר לְךָ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וְכִי מִיכַל יָלְדָה? וַהֲלֹא מֵירַב יָלְדָה! מֵירַב יָלְדָה וּמִיכַל גִּידְּלָה, לְפִיכָךְ נִקְרְאוּ עַל שְׁמָהּ. לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁכׇּל הַמְגַדֵּל יָתוֹם בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ יְלָדוֹ.
licence_note: Sefaria: 'William Davidson Edition - Vocalized Aramaic', licence CC-BY-NC. Do not reproduce without attribution and NC restriction. Own translation below (team).
own_translation_en: R. Yehoshua ben Korha also raised the same difficulty: 'Is it not written, "the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul"?' R. Yehoshua answered him: 'Did Michal bear them? Surely Merab bore them! Merab bore them and Michal raised them; therefore they were called by her name. This teaches that anyone who raises an orphan in his house, Scripture counts him as though he had begotten him.'
from_: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה נָמֵי, הָכְתִיב:
to: בֵּיתוֹ מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ יְלָדוֹ.
what_it_shows: R. Yehoshua ben Korha answers the objection to 'the five sons of Michal': Merab bore them and Michal raised them, so they are called by Michal's name. The verse teaches that anyone who raises an orphan in his house, Scripture regards as though he had begotten him.
context: Talmudic discussion of David's marriages to Merab and Michal (19b). Sefaria's Koren text, element 12 of the Sefaria v3 API read.
limits: (1) This is rabbinic exegesis of a textual problem (the verse's 'bore'), not a legal ruling on tribe, land or inheritance. (2) The principle concerns the child's name and the foster-parent's status ('as though he had begotten him'), not the child's tribe or the Davidic line. (3) The same sugya discusses the validity of Merab's and Michal's betrothals ('betrothal by error') and other readings (R. Yose; the question of how David married two sisters); I read only elements 2-6 and 11-12 of the Sefaria text, not the full sugya. (4) Sefaria's version here is CC-BY-NC (Koren vocalization); the Vilna edition was not reachable.

quote_orig: כִּֽי־יֵשְׁב֨וּ אַחִ֜ים יַחְדָּ֗ו וּמֵ֨ת אַחַ֤ד מֵהֶם֙ וּבֵ֣ן אֵֽין־ל֔וֹ לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֧ה אֵֽשֶׁת־הַמֵּ֛ת הַח֖וּצָה לְאִ֣ישׁ זָ֑ר יְבָמָהּ֙ יָבֹ֣א עָלֶ֔יהָ וּלְקָחָ֥הּ ל֛וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֖ה וְיִבְּמָֽהּ׃ וְהָיָ֗ה הַבְּכוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּלֵ֔ד יָק֕וּם עַל־שֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו הַמֵּ֑ת וְלֹֽא־יִמָּחֶ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
quote_en: If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not be married abroad unto one not of his kin; her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto her. And it shall be, that the first-born that she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother that is dead, that his name be not blotted out of Israel.
from_: If brethren dwell together, and one of
to: name be not blotted out of Israel.
keys: וְהָיָ֗ה הַבְּכוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּלֵ֔ד יָק֕וּם עַל־שֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו הַמֵּ֑ת
what_it_shows: Levirate rule: if brothers dwell together and one dies childless, the living brother takes the widow; 'the first-born that she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother that is dead, that his name be not blotted out of Israel'.
context: Deut 25:5-10 (read): the levirate rule with the refusal ceremony (shoe and spitting; 25:9-10).
limits: (1) The text speaks of the name ('shem') only: it does not mention tribe, land or inheritance. (2) The child is the living brother's blood child (25:5: 'her husband's brother shall go in unto her'), reckoned in the dead man's name. This is a naming fiction, not a transfer of lineage to a non-blood person. (3) The refusal ceremony (25:7-10, read) shows the rule was enforced by the elders and can be refused.

quote_orig: וְגַ֣ם אֶת־ר֣וּת הַמֹּאֲבִיָּה֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת מַחְל֜וֹן קָנִ֧יתִי לִ֣י לְאִשָּׁ֗ה לְהָקִ֤ים שֵׁם־הַמֵּת֙ עַל־נַ֣חֲלָת֔וֹ וְלֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֧ת שֵׁם־הַמֵּ֛ת מֵעִ֥ם אֶחָ֖יו וּמִשַּׁ֣עַר מְקוֹמ֑וֹ עֵדִ֥ים אַתֶּ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃
quote_en: Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I acquired to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place; ye are witnesses this day.’
from_: Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of
to: his place; ye are witnesses this day.’
what_it_shows: Boaz says he has acquired Ruth the Moabitess 'to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren'. The verse links the name to the dead man's inheritance.
context: Boaz's transaction with the nearer kinsman at the gate (4:1-10). The kinsman has declined (4:6, read).
limits: (1) 4:6 (read): the nearer kinsman refuses 'lest I mar mine own inheritance'. The redemption/levirate child would take the dead man's inheritance and cost the redeemer his own. (2) The child's paternity is Boaz's: 'she bore a son' (4:13, read) and 'Boaz begot Obed' (4:21, read). 'Raising up the name' is a naming-and-inheritance fiction. (3) 4:7 (read) calls the shoe-custom 'the custom in former time'.

quote_orig: וַתִּקַּ֨ח נׇעֳמִ֤י אֶת־הַיֶּ֙לֶד֙ וַתְּשִׁתֵ֣הוּ בְחֵיקָ֔הּ וַתְּהִי־ל֖וֹ לְאֹמֶֽנֶת׃ וַתִּקְרֶ֩אנָה֩ ל֨וֹ הַשְּׁכֵנ֥וֹת שֵׁם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יֻלַּד־בֵּ֖ן לְנׇעֳמִ֑י וַתִּקְרֶ֤אנָֽה שְׁמוֹ֙ עוֹבֵ֔ד ה֥וּא אֲבִֽי־יִשַׁ֖י אֲבִ֥י דָוִֽד׃
quote_en: And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it. And the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying: ‘There is a son born to Naomi’; and they called his name Obed; he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
from_: And Naomi took the child, and laid
to: father of Jesse, the father of David.
what_it_shows: Naomi takes the child and 'became nurse unto it'; the neighbour women give it a name: 'There is a son born to Naomi'; they call him Obed, 'the father of Jesse, the father of David'.
context: After Boaz and Ruth's marriage and the birth (4:13). The verse ends the story and leads to the genealogy (4:18-22).
limits: The genealogy (4:18-22, read) says 'Boaz begot Obed' (4:21): the child is Boaz's blood son in the lineage. The naming ('a son is born to Naomi') is by neighbours and gives Naomi a claim by name and care only. Name and genealogy diverge in this text.

quote_orig: לָ֣מָּה יִגָּרַ֤ע שֵׁם־אָבִ֙ינוּ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֔וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ בֵּ֑ן תְּנָה־לָּ֣נוּ אֲחֻזָּ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲחֵ֥י אָבִֽינוּ׃
quote_en: Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he had no son? Give unto us a possession among the brethren of our father.’
from_: Why should the name of our father
to: possession among the brethren of our father.’
what_it_shows: The daughters of Zelophehad ask: 'Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he had no son?' The LORD grants that daughters inherit (27:7-8, read: 'If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter').
context: The daughters of Zelophehad, of the clan of Manasseh (27:1). The rule is a law about inheritance when there is no son.
limits: (1) This is inheritance by blood (daughters of the dead man), not adoption. (2) Num 36:6-9 (read): 'So shall no inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe; for the children of Israel shall cleave every one to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.' Daughters must marry within their father's tribe. Tribal inheritance does not move by legal or other means.

quote_orig: וְיָאִ֤יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁה֙ הָלַ֔ךְ וַיִּלְכֹּ֖ד אֶת־חַוֺּתֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶתְהֶ֖ן חַוֺּ֥ת יָאִֽיר׃
quote_en: And Jair the son of Manasseh went and took the villages thereof, and called them Havvoth-jair.
from_: And Jair the son of Manasseh went
to: the villages thereof, and called them Havvoth-jair.
what_it_shows: 'Jair the son of Manasseh' took the villages of Gilead and called them Havvoth-jair. Deut 3:14 (read) repeats the designation.
context: Settlement of the trans-Jordan tribes (Num 32). Jair's identity is given as Manassite.
limits: 1 Chr 2:21-22 (read): Hezron (Judah's line, 2:9 read) took 'the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead' and bore Segub, and Segub begot Jair (2:22). So Jair's paternal line is Judah; the Manassite identity comes through Machir (his mother's family). 2:23 (read) says 'All these were the sons of Machir the father of Gilead', whose referent is ambiguous. The text states the identity but not the mechanism; it does not say adoption.

quote_orig: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן שֵׁשָׁ֧ן אֶת־בִּתּ֛וֹ לְיַרְחָ֥ע עַבְדּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד ל֖וֹ אֶת־עַתָּֽי׃ וְעַתַּי֙ הֹלִ֣יד אֶת־נָתָ֔ן וְנָתָ֖ן הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־זָבָֽד׃
quote_en: So Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife; and she bore him Attai. And Attai begot Nathan, and Nathan begot Zabad;
from_: So Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha
to: Attai begot Nathan, and Nathan begot Zabad;
what_it_shows: Sheshan 'had no sons, but daughters'; he gives his daughter to Jarha, an Egyptian servant, who bears Attai; 'And Attai begot Nathan'.
context: Genealogy of Judah in the Chronicler (2:34-36, with 2:34 'Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters').
limits: (1) The text never says adoption. The line passes through the daughter: Attai's father is the Egyptian servant Jarha (2:35). (2) The Egyptian origin is explicit and the line continues in the genealogy (2:36, read); the verse does not say Attai is reckoned as Sheshan's son. (3) It is a case of a line through a daughter, not an outsider adopted by a non-relative.

quote_orig: וַיִּגְּשׁ֨וּ בְנֵי־יְהוּדָ֤ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ בַּגִּלְגָּ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו כָּלֵ֥ב בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּ֖ה הַקְּנִזִּ֑י אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֡עְתָּ אֶֽת־הַדָּבָר֩ אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים עַ֧ל אֹדוֹתַ֛י וְעַ֥ל אֹדוֹתֶ֖יךָ בְּקָדֵ֥שׁ בַּרְנֵֽעַ׃
quote_en: Then the children of Judah drew nigh unto Joshua in Gilgal; and Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said unto him: ‘Thou knowest the thing that the LORD spoke unto Moses the man of God concerning me and concerning thee in Kadesh-barnea.
from_: Then the children of Judah drew nigh
to: concerning me and concerning thee in Kadesh-barnea.
what_it_shows: 'The children of Judah' come to Joshua, and 'Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite' speaks for himself, asking for Hebron (14:6-14, read).
context: Allotment of Judah; Caleb asks for his promised inheritance (14:6-14).
limits: (1) Num 13:6 (read): 'Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh'; Num 32:12 (read): 'Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite'. (2) Gen 36:11, 36:15, 36:42 (read) list Kenaz among Esau's (Edomite) descendants and chiefs. (3) Judg 1:13 (read): 'Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother'. The Kenaz relation to Caleb's father is not explained. (4) 1 Chr 2:18 (read) calls Caleb 'son of Hezron', a different identification. The text does not explain how a Kenizzite came to belong to Judah; no adoption is mentioned.

quote_orig: וַיֵּ֩שֶׁב֩ אֲר֨וֹן יְהֹוָ֜ה בֵּ֣ית עֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֛ם הַגִּתִּ֖י שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֑ים וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶת־עֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֖ם וְאֶת־כׇּל־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃
quote_en: And the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months; and the LORD blessed Obed-edom, and all his house.
from_: And the ark of the LORD remained
to: LORD blessed Obed-edom, and all his house.
what_it_shows: The ark of the LORD stays three months in the house of Obed-edom 'the Gittite', and 'the LORD blessed Obed-edom, and all his house'.
context: The ark's transfer to Jerusalem (2 Sam 6:10-11; parallel 1 Chr 13:13-14, read).
limits: (1) The Samuel and Chronicles (1 Chr 13:13, read) accounts call him 'the Gittite' (a gentilic, not an adoption). (2) 1 Chr 16:38 (read): 'Obed-edom also the son of Jedithun and Hosah to be door-keepers'; 1 Chr 15:18, 15:24 (read) list him among the gatekeepers; 1 Chr 26:4-8 (read) gives his sons and kin, 'able men'. (3) No adoption or incorporation is stated; the Chronicler gives him a Levitical father, a different identification from the Samuel account.

quote_orig: וּמִבְּנֵי֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים בְּנֵ֥י חֳבַיָּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י הַקּ֑וֹץ בְּנֵ֣י בַרְזִלַּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָ֠קַ֠ח מִבְּנ֞וֹת בַּרְזִלַּ֤י הַגִּלְעָדִי֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה וַיִּקָּרֵ֖א עַל־שְׁמָֽם׃ אֵ֗לֶּה בִּקְשׁ֧וּ כְתָבָ֛ם הַמִּתְיַחְשִׂ֖ים וְלֹ֣א נִמְצָ֑אוּ וַֽיְגֹאֲל֖וּ מִן־הַכְּהֻנָּֽה׃
quote_en: And of the children of the priests: the children of Habaiah, the children of Hakkoz, the children of Barzillai, who took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name. These sought their register, that is, the genealogy, but it was not found; therefore were they deemed polluted and put from the priesthood.
from_: And of the children of the priests:
to: deemed polluted and put from the priesthood.
keys: אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָ֠קַ֠ח מִבְּנ֞וֹת בַּרְזִלַּ֤י הַגִּלְעָדִי֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה
what_it_shows: Priests' families: the sons of Barzillai, 'who took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name'. They sought their register and it was not found, so they were 'put from the priesthood'.
context: Ezra 2:61-62 (read in Sefaria's JPS 1917 text), within the list of priests. Neh 7:63-64 (read) has the same text.
limits: (1) The naming by a wife's family did not confer priestly status: 2:62 says they could not show their genealogical register and were excluded from the priesthood. Descent records decided priestly lineage. (2) The Hebrew 'וַיִּקָּרֵא עַל־שְׁמָם' leaves the grammatical subject ambiguous (who was called by whose name). (3) This is a naming-through-marriage case, not an adoption.
